newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Diffs firm, MTBE holds its muscle.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Diffs firm, MTBE holds its muscle.

text.p: U.S. cash gasoline differentials firmed in quiet trade on Monday as players digested news of progress in Iraq's second round of "oil-for-food" sales and MTBE held its muscle.

On NYMEX, crude oil futures reversed midday after a firm opening, down 10 cents at $19.79 a barrel. August gasoline futures were up 1.82 cents at 64.03 cents a gallon and heating oil was up 0.60 points at 53.99 cents.
Gasoline differentials remained firm in New York riding a continuing wave of strength in MTBE markets.

"Clearly MTBE has the major role," said one East Coast gasoline trader. "Octane and RFG are still really strong," he said, referring to premium and reformulated grades that are typically blended with MTBE to raise either octane or oxygen.

There were a few bearish voices among traders, but for the moment they were in the minority, with the question of when additional cargoes of both finished gasoline and MTBE might arrive one of the big disagreements between bulls and bears.

For the moment the "A2" regular northern-grade reformulated held its value, with prompt barrels still offered at about 2.25 cents over, and barrels for delivery by the beginning of next month heard offered at 2.00 cents over.

The "V2" and "D2" 93-octane conventional and reformulated northern blends also held their strength, with prompt barrels of both grades offered as high as 7.25 and 11.50 cents over August NYMEX unleaded.

Midcontinent conventional unleaded gasoline differentials edged upward amid a slight tail off in days of supply. Traders said supply eased from 20-days last week to 19-days this week, but plenty of barrels were seen coming for next week.
"We have lower days of supply and futures came off but we do have lots of stuff coming next week in the system," said a trader, referring to 0.25 cent rise in Group Three.
Group Three unleaded was pegged at 0.50 to 0.25 cent below the print, with the any months on par.
Chicago markets, which were now quoting August barrels, were pegged at 3.00 cents over the print for August 1 to 10 delivery. The any months were 1.00/1.25 cents over the September screen.
Trade in the U.S. Gulf started off on a quiet note, a continuation of late last week when many players were away for a BP-sponsored golf outing. Gasoline differentials, however, held their strength.

One trader said the cash gasoline market was stepping back to see how the Iraq news fully shakes out. The U.N. on Monday confirmed the start date for Iraqi oil sales was June 8, which means the country will have to sell 1.5 million to 2 million barrels per day to meet its quota by the Sept 5 deadline.
On Monday, U.S. Gulf M1-grade was a quarter cent stronger at 0.50 to 0.25 cents under the print. Differentials firmed late last week on buying by Star Enterprise.
Prompt A1-grade reformulated 93-octane firmed about a quarter cent to 2.50/3.00 cents over the print on tight supply but V1-grade remained steady with sellers at 6.00 cents over the screen.
